title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a typed page from a seminar exposé, headed '- 28 - IX' and stamped 346. It is not part of the handwritten divided-power De Rham notes on the neighbouring pages, which concern the automorphism group scheme Ω of the completed simplicial divided-power differential algebra. Its content (kernels _nK of multiplication by n, a group G that may be smooth, H of finite presentation, Proposition 3.1 a)) matches the style of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'). I am unsure of the exact numbering there.

Lemma 3.1.3, first assertion. Let S be a scheme and K → S quasi-finite, of finite presentation, separated and flat. Let s ∈ S and let t be a generization of s. Then rank K_s ≤ rank K_t, where rank means the k(s)-dimension of the finite k(s)-scheme K_s. In other words, fibre degree is lower semicontinuous under generization.
- Proof: reduce by strict localisation to S strictly local (strictly henselian local).
- Then K splits as K^f ⊔ K', with K^f finite over S and K' having empty special fibre (EGA IV 18.5.11 type decomposition).
- K^f is finite, flat and of finite presentation, hence locally free, so its rank is constant: rank K_s = rank K^f_s = rank K^f_t ≤ rank K_t.

Second assertion. If rank K_η ≤ 1 at every maximal point η of S, then K → S is an open immersion. In particular it is an isomorphism if it has a section.
- Proof: every s generizes to some maximal point, so rank K_s ≤ 1 for all s. Hence each K_s is empty or equal to Spec k(s).
- So K → S is a monomorphism, by the fibrewise criterion for monomorphisms locally of finite type (cited as SGA 3 VI_B 2.11; compare EGA IV 17.2.6).
- A flat monomorphism of finite presentation is an open immersion (EGA IV 17.9.1).

Remark 3.1.4 begins to explain the role of the lemma. Proposition 3.1 a) says nothing about _nK_s when n is a power of the residue characteristic p. For G smooth (and S locally noetherian, or H of finite presentation), one can still say something by the same method. The lemma is the tool that bounds kernels fibrewise via generic fibres, as in Néron-model and monodromy arguments.
errors: Typo in the original typescript: 't ∈ T' should read 't ∈ S'.
Minor: 'rang K_s ≤ 1 implies K_s empty or Spec k(s)' uses that rank is the degree over k(s), not the number of points. This is the intended meaning, so it is correct as written.

ideas.what: Lower semicontinuity of fibre degree for flat, separated, quasi-finite morphisms of finite presentation, proved via the strictly henselian splitting into a finite part plus a part with empty special fibre.
ideas.modern_name: Upper/lower semicontinuity of fibre degree for quasi-finite flat morphisms; structure of quasi-finite separated schemes over a henselian base.
ideas.where_published: Probably SGA 7 I Exp. IX (LNM 288); ingredients in EGA IV 18.5.11

ideas.what: A flat monomorphism of finite presentation is an open immersion; fibrewise criterion for monomorphisms.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a typed page of an already published SGA-style exposé (most likely SGA 7 IX), filed among the divided-power De Rham notes. Its content is a standard lemma with a correct, routine proof. The only point of interest is archival: a misfiled typescript page.
transcription_corrections: The transcription is faithful. 't ∈ T' is a typo in the original typescript itself, not a transcription error.
The marginal '176' is the archive folio number and '346' is a later page stamp; neither is part of the text.
